title: Knee Line
shortDefinition: The knee line is the boundary that decides whether the leg is controlled in an entanglement or free.
whyItMatters: In leg locks, trapped knee line plus heel exposure is a major danger signal.
deepExplanation: Knee line is a safety concept before it is an attacking concept. Do not rotate hard while knee line is trapped. When attacking, controlling it prevents leg withdrawal.
beginnerView: Know whether your knee is trapped or free before turning.
advancedView: Use knee line to evaluate sweep, pass, leg entry, and safety at the same time.

ifThenExamples.if: If you lose Knee Line during the exchange.
ifThenExamples.then: Stop accelerating, recover the nearest body structure, then continue the technique.
ifThenExamples.why: Modern no-gi punishes forceful continuation after structure is lost.

ifThenExamples.if: If the opponent correctly answers your first line.
ifThenExamples.then: Use Knee Line to switch to a safer branch instead of forcing the same line.
ifThenExamples.why: A good concept turns the opponent’s reaction into information for the next decision.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Knee Line is a single technical trick.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: Treat it as a decision rule that appears across many positions.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Understanding the concept automatically makes it work live.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: The concept needs body signals, short cues, and positional rolling.

trainingCues: Name Knee Line before adding force.
Find the body signal instead of guessing generally.
If structure is lost, reset one layer first.
Drill slowly, then test with progressive resistance.
